item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","shard_id":"8B-S06","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0049-E012","BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E003","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E008","BATCH-0050-E009","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0050-E013","BATCH-0050-E014","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0050-E016","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E003","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0051-E011","BATCH-0051-E012","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E016","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0051-E018","BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0051-E020","BATCH-0051-E021","BATCH-0051-E022","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0051-E024","BATCH-0051-E026","BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E003","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E005","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0052-E007","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0052-E011","BATCH-0052-E012"],"answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"The shard provides clear evidence of an explicit program. López Obrador’s 2018 platform identified austerity, anti-corruption, poverty reduction, social programs, peace, energy and food self-sufficiency, infrastructure, and a state-led development model. The 2023 priority-program portfolio also established formal objectives, although several programs had ambiguous or management-oriented purposes and some objectives became less clear over time.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E011","BATCH-0051-E012","BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0051-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0051-E024","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The programmatic baseline predates 2023.","Several program objectives lacked clearly defined target populations, intended changes, or results orientation.","Some evidence concerns federal programs rather than López Obrador’s personal decisions."]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"The administration translated major priorities into budgets, institutions, operating rules, infrastructure projects, security arrangements, and program machinery. Examples include expanded social-program budgets, IMSS-BIENESTAR’s 2023 rules, the Maya Train and military operating structure, centralized medicine procurement, and energy reforms. Operationalization was uneven: some programs lacked clear rules or accountability, several objectives were poorly specified, and major energy reform failed to obtain the required legislative majority.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E008","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E003","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E014","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0051-E024","BATCH-0052-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal rules and budgets do not establish effective execution.","Some policy choices were made by ministries, Congress, or agencies rather than demonstrably by the president personally.","The Baker evidence is partly predictive."]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"The shard shows substantial mobilization of administrative and financial resources toward social programs, health federalization, infrastructure, energy, and security. Social-program budgets expanded materially; IMSS-BIENESTAR specified national administrative, financial, staffing, supervision, and reporting structures; and the administration deployed the military in security and infrastructure roles. Mobilization was mixed because resources were concentrated unevenly, some programs lacked adequate monitoring, and austerity and centralization generated capacity and service problems.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E016","BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0052-E003","BATCH-0052-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E009","BATCH-0050-E014","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0052-E003","BATCH-0052-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Budget allocation and formal administrative structures are not equivalent to effective mobilization.","Military, international, subnational, and agency contributions complicate presidential attribution.","Execution evidence is stronger for selected programs than for the whole governing portfolio."]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"The evidence shows deliberate use of personnel structures, including nearly 20,000 social-program field workers, federal health leadership and multidisciplinary supervisory teams, trained health personnel, and expanded military roles. However, the shard does not provide a systematic assessment of whether López Obrador selected, retained, or replaced capable implementers across the full program portfolio. It also records staffing shortages and concerns that loyalists and military operators were favored over independent institutional capacity.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E016","BATCH-0051-E019"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0050-E016","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E018","BATCH-0051-E019"],"limitations_and_gaps":["There is little direct evidence of individual appointment quality or replacement decisions.","Formal training and organizational roles do not prove competence in practice.","Some personnel attribution is to agencies or military institutions rather than the ruler."]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination and territorial reach are documented in the social and health systems: IMSS-BIENESTAR specified central, regional, hospital, and zonal structures, regular visits, commitments, reporting, and coordination with states and other institutions; social programs used national administrative networks; and the government deployed troops and workers during the Acapulco crisis. Follow-through was inconsistent, with shortages, incomplete registries, weak program indicators, environmental and contractor disputes, and uneven crisis assistance.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0052-E011","BATCH-0052-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0049-E012","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E008","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0052-E005","BATCH-0052-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Many coordination mechanisms are prescribed rather than independently verified.","Territorial compliance and milestone completion are not comprehensively documented.","The Acapulco evidence covers only the early aftermath."]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"The shard contains substantial evidence that programs became institutional practice: social transfers were delivered directly, budgets and beneficiaries expanded, IMSS-BIENESTAR issued mandatory operating rules and service requirements, health and social programs established monitoring structures, and major infrastructure projects advanced. At the same time, CONEVAL found that some programs did not measure results or had unclear objectives, medicine shortages worsened, health access deteriorated, and some projects faced environmental and legal disputes.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E003","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E008","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E003","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0052-E005","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0052-E007","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0052-E011","BATCH-0052-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0049-E012","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E009","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0050-E016","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0051-E018","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0051-E024","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal implementation and output measures do not establish service quality or causal success.","Several outcome and coverage measures are from 2021 or 2022 rather than 2023.","Some adverse project claims are allegations or analytical assessments rather than final adjudications."]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Progress toward selected goals was mixed. Social-program reach and budgets expanded; poverty and inequality indicators improved through 2022, and some programs met or exceeded coverage and target measures. However, attribution is shared with wage policy, remittances, and other factors; health access, education lag, medicine availability, security, energy self-sufficiency, and economic performance showed serious weaknesses. Several program indicators were missing, deficient, or based on targets rather than independent outcomes.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E003","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E021","BATCH-0051-E022","BATCH-0052-E005","BATCH-0052-E007","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0052-E011","BATCH-0052-E023"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E009","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0050-E016","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0051-E018","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0051-E024","BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E003","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most outcome evidence ends before the end of 2023.","Causal contribution is not isolated from external shocks, remittances, wage changes, pandemic effects, global energy prices, criminal actors, or joint programs.","Program CEM and coverage metrics measure stated targets and indicators, not necessarily durable welfare impact."]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"The shard shows that monitoring, evaluation, supervision, and corrective mechanisms were formally established, especially in IMSS-BIENESTAR, including audits, dashboards, external evaluations, commitments, and corrective actions. There is some evidence of program redesign and indicator changes. But CONEVAL reported that recommendations were disregarded to varying degrees, several programs retained weak or absent results measurement, and the shard supplies little direct evidence that López Obrador personally used audits to replace implementers or reallocate resources in response to failure.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E003","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0052-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0051-E024","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The IMSS-BIENESTAR rules prescribe adaptation mechanisms but do not report their operation or findings.","No systematic evidence identifies presidential responses to failed programs.","Recommendations being disregarded is not quantified by program or attributed personally."]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"The ruler’s crisis and resistance management preserved some priorities but produced mixed execution. The administration mobilized troops and workers after Hurricane Otis, maintained social programs during the pandemic, pursued energy and security objectives despite opposition, and used legal and institutional strategies to advance its political agenda. Conversely, early disaster aid was uneven, security outcomes deteriorated, international energy disputes persisted, and courts, Congress, civil society, and opposition constrained or invalidated parts of the agenda.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E003","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0050-E014","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0051-E020","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0052-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0049-E012","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E016","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0051-E018","BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0051-E020"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The Otis report covers the early response and cannot assess reconstruction.","Several political and international assessments are analytical or predictive.","Crisis outcomes reflect external shocks, criminal organizations, courts, Congress, civil society, and foreign governments as well as presidential decisions."]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By the end of the period, the administration had converted substantial parts of its program into durable budgets, social-transfer institutions, operating rules, military responsibilities, and major infrastructure commitments. Some social outcomes improved and certain administrative capacities strengthened. Durability and overall goal achievement remained mixed: health and education systems weakened, security and energy goals showed adverse outcomes, several programs lacked clear results measurement, major projects had cost and environmental concerns, and institutional changes faced judicial and political resistance.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E016","BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0052-E003","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0052-E011","BATCH-0052-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0049-E012","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E008","BATCH-0050-E009","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0050-E013","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0050-E016","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0051-E018","BATCH-0051-E020","BATCH-0051-E024","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E005","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0052-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide a complete end-of-2023 assessment across every program component.","Durability beyond the administration is only partly observable and often projected.","Attribution is mixed among the president, agencies, Congress, military, subnational governments, international partners, and external conditions."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["This shard is evidence-only and does not support a chapter score.","Several items are duplicates, forecasts, formal program rules, or joint-government/international outputs; they should not be treated as independent confirmation without accounting for source dependence.","Moral effects and human-rights harms are preserved as evidence about execution, crisis management, and goal advancement but should not be converted into a moral judgment within the effectiveness chapter."]}
